# The Comment-Free Copy and the Original: What They Share, How They Differ

Original: `/mnt/kaun/wow-chat-2026`. Copy: `/mnt/kaun/wow-chat-2026-intuition` (pushed to `https://github.com/gabrilend/wow-chat-2026.git`, branch `intuition`).
Both compared at commit `25d1f8c76`, the one the copy was last made from
(2026-11-03 11:54:10). Issue 190 says why the copy exists; `strategems/intuition-copy.md` describes the pattern.

## What they share

- **The same files at the same paths**: 1179 of the commit's 2610 files are in both, under the same
  names in the same folders, so a path found in one is found in the other.
- **The same code**: in the 1022 files that differ, only comments were taken out; every
  statement, string and setting is as in the original, so both run the same way
  (`scripts/test-make-intuition-copy` checks every Lua file compiles, every shell
  script parses, and every install marker the installer reads is still there).
- **Byte for byte the same**: 157 files (data, pictures, JSON, files with no comments,
  and 11 symbolic links).
- **The same history point**: the copy's receipt names the original's commit, and each of
  the copy's own commits (4 so far) is named after the commit it came from.

## What only the copy has

- `CLAUDE.md`: not the project's instructions but the same short default every intuition copy
  gets (`strategems/intuition-copy-CLAUDE.md`): look in the scripts folder for common actions,
  and learn the project in the order the build takes in its sources.
- `.intuition-copy`: the receipt, naming the source commit and what was done.
- `.intuition-report.md`: this report, rewritten with every update of the copy.
- Its own git history, pushed as the `intuition` branch of the original's repository; it is
  updated before each push of the original's main branch (`scripts/install-intuition-push-hook`),
  with only the files that changed.

All the files only in the copy, counted: `.intuition-copy`, `.intuition-report.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.

## What this means for an agent in each

- In the original, an agent reads why things are as they are: the issues, the owner's words,
  the summaries beside each file, the comments. It learns the project's own names and
  framing, its mistakes included.
- In the copy, the same code with none of that: an agent learns from what runs, in the
  order the build runs it. Where the two agents agree, the understanding is confirmed from
  two directions; where they differ, a comment has gone stale, or the reasoning in the
  record went somewhere the code does not.
